plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their behavior, since your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win). Bidding above value risks winning at a loss; bidding below value risks losing a profitable opportunity. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $37 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction, where the winner pays the second-highest bid rather than their own bid. In this format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value ($17). Bidding higher risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me if I'm the second-highest bidder's price. Bidding lower risks losing an auction I could have profitably won. Since my payment depends on others' bids, not my own, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy: you win exactly when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're highest). Overbidding risks paying more than value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With value $46, the optimal action is to bid truthfully at $46, maximizing expected profit given the auction's incentive structure.
